claims.text: A combined high-throughput CALPHAD and high-temperature experimental protocol can determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties for single-phase HEAs.
The combined protocol can achieve an average error below 10%.
Near-equiatomic, homogeneous, single-phase FCC or BCC HEAs can be synthesized by conventional casting or additive manufacturing.
High-throughput CALPHAD calculations can predict fusion thermodynamics in HEAs.
Experimental validation can refine CALPHAD predictions and thermodynamic databases for HEAs.
Inert or reducing environments minimize oxidation during high-temperature HEA measurements.
Near-equilibrium conditions, controlled heating rates, and calibrated instruments reduce non-equilibrium and measurement errors.
Controlled, homogeneous single-phase microstructures minimize compositional segregation and non-equilibrium effects.
The high configurational entropy of HEAs produces predictable trends in fusion properties.
Calibrated CALPHAD models can capture the configurational-entropy-related trends in HEA fusion properties.
Precision experiments refine simulation parameters and thereby reduce uncertainty in predicted fusion properties.
Integrating high-throughput thermodynamic computation with experimental validation is an efficient approach for HEA research.
Predicted fusion properties will match direct measurements within 10% across the compositional space of HEAs.
Traditional measurements in binary or ternary alloys typically exhibit 10–15% experimental scatter.
Significant microsegregation, compositional inhomogeneity, or metastable phases during melting reduce the reliability of the proposed approach.
When microsegregation, compositional inhomogeneity, or metastable phases dominate, errors may exceed 10%.
Liquid-phase interaction models for multicomponent HEAs may require further refinement.
Calibrated DSC across controlled heating rates can quantify fusion enthalpy and entropy.
High-precision dilatometry can quantify volume change at melting.
Equilibrium phase analysis can quantify liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis is restricted to single-phase HEAs, whereas the predicted outcome claims performance across the full compositional space of HEAs; the boundary then excludes or weakens performance for compositions exhibiting segregation or metastable phases.

The hypothesis specifies average error below 10%, the predicted outcome implies results within 10% across the compositional space, but the falsification rule only rejects the approach when more than half of compositions exceed 10%. Thus, substantial failure of the stated performance target might not satisfy the stated falsification criterion.
